title: Erlkönig
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_notes: German text from Goethe's 1782 ballad; English translation by Edgar Alfred Bowring, 1853.
reading_notes: A father rides through dark woods with his feverish child, who sees the Elf-King beckoning. The Elf-King's voice alternates with the father's consolations and the child's terror. Schubert set the poem famously to music. Three voices live in the same lines: father, son, king.

lines.original: Wer reitet so spät durch Nacht und Wind?
lines.english: Who rides there so late through the night dark and drear?
lines.gloss: Wer = 'who' (nominative); reitet = 'rides' (3rd sg. of reiten); so spät = 'so late'; durch = 'through' (+accusative); Nacht = 'night' (accusative); Wind = 'wind' (accusative).

lines.original: Es ist der Vater mit seinem Kind;
lines.english: The father it is, with his infant so dear;
lines.gloss: Es ist = 'it is'; der Vater = 'the father' (nominative); mit = 'with' (+dative); seinem Kind = 'his child' (dative neuter).

lines.original: Er hat den Knaben wohl in dem Arm,
lines.english: He holdeth the boy tightly clasp'd in his arm,
lines.gloss: Er = 'he'; hat = 'has'; den Knaben = 'the boy' (accusative); wohl = 'well, indeed'; in dem Arm = 'in the arm' (dative, location).

lines.original: Er faßt ihn sicher, er hält ihn warm.
lines.english: He holdeth him safely, he keepeth him warm.
lines.gloss: faßt = 'grasps' (fassen); ihn = 'him' (accusative); sicher = 'safely'; hält = 'holds' (halten); warm = 'warm'.

lines.original: "Mein Sohn, was birgst du so bang dein Gesicht?"
lines.english: "My son, wherefore seek'st thou thy face thus to hide?"
lines.gloss: Mein Sohn = 'my son' (vocative); was = 'why'; birgst = 'hidest' (2nd sg. of bergen); du = 'thou'; so bang = 'so anxiously'; dein Gesicht = 'thy face' (accusative).

lines.original: "Siehst, Vater, du den Erlkönig nicht?
lines.english: "Look, father, the Erl-King is close by our side!
lines.gloss: Siehst = 'seest' (sehen); Vater = 'father' (vocative); du = 'thou'; den Erlkönig = 'the Erl-King' (accusative); nicht = 'not'.

lines.original: Den Erlenkönig mit Kron und Schweif?"
lines.english: Dost see not the Erl-King, with crown and with train?"
lines.gloss: Den Erlenkönig = 'the Alder-King' (accusative); mit = 'with' (+dative); Kron = 'crown' (poetic for Krone); Schweif = 'train, tail' (dative).

lines.original: "Mein Sohn, es ist ein Nebelstreif."
lines.english: "My son, 'tis the mist rising over the plain."
lines.gloss: es ist = 'it is'; ein Nebelstreif = 'a streak of mist' (nominative).

lines.original: "Du liebes Kind, komm, geh mit mir!
lines.english: "Oh, come, thou dear infant! oh come thou with me!
lines.gloss: Du = 'thou'; liebes Kind = 'dear child' (vocative); komm = 'come!' (imperative); geh = 'go!' (imperative of gehen); mit mir = 'with me' (dative).

lines.original: Gar schöne Spiele spiel' ich mit dir;
lines.english: Full many a game I will play there with thee;
lines.gloss: Gar = 'very, truly'; schöne Spiele = 'beautiful games' (accusative plural); spiel' = 'I play' (contraction spiele); ich = 'I'; mit dir = 'with thee' (dative).

lines.original: Manch' bunte Blumen sind an dem Strand,
lines.english: On the shore many flowers of hue are unrolling,
lines.gloss: Manch' = 'many a' (contraction of manche); bunte = 'colorful'; Blumen = 'flowers' (nominative plural); sind = 'are'; an dem Strand = 'on the shore' (dative).

lines.original: Meine Mutter hat manch gülden Gewand."
lines.english: My mother hath many a garment of gold."
lines.gloss: Meine Mutter = 'my mother' (nominative); hat = 'has'; manch = 'many a'; gülden = 'golden' (poetic form of golden); Gewand = 'garment' (accusative, neuter).

lines.original: "Mein Vater, mein Vater, und hörest du nicht,
lines.english: "My father, my father, and dost thou not hear
lines.gloss: Mein Vater = 'my father' (vocative, repeated); hörest = 'hearest' (archaic 2nd sg. of hören); du = 'thou'; nicht = 'not'.

lines.original: Was Erlenkönig mir leise verspricht?"
lines.english: The words that the Erl-King now breathes in mine ear?"
lines.gloss: Was = 'what' (relative); mir = 'to me' (dative); leise = 'softly'; verspricht = 'promises' (versprechen).

lines.original: "Sei ruhig, bleibe ruhig, mein Kind;
lines.english: "Be calm, dearest child, 'tis thy fancy deceives;
lines.gloss: Sei = 'be!' (imperative of sein); ruhig = 'calm'; bleibe = 'remain!' (imperative of bleiben); mein Kind = 'my child' (vocative).

lines.original: In dürren Blättern säuselt der Wind."
lines.english: 'Tis the sad wind that sighs through the withering leaves."
lines.gloss: In = 'in' (+dative); dürren = 'dry, withered' (dative plural); Blättern = 'leaves' (dative plural of Blatt); säuselt = 'rustles, sighs' (säuseln); der Wind = 'the wind' (nominative).

lines.original: "Willst, feiner Knabe, du mit mir gehn?
lines.english: "Wilt go, then, dear infant, wilt go with me there?
lines.gloss: Willst = 'wilt' (wollen); feiner Knabe = 'fair boy' (vocative); mit mir = 'with me' (dative); gehn = 'to go' (infinitive, contracted).

lines.original: Meine Töchter sollen dich warten schön;
lines.english: My daughters shall tend thee with sisterly care;
lines.gloss: Meine Töchter = 'my daughters' (nominative plural); sollen = 'shall' (modal); dich = 'thee' (accusative); warten = 'to attend, wait upon' (+accusative here poetic); schön = 'beautifully'.

lines.original: Meine Töchter führen den nächtlichen Reihn,
lines.english: My daughters by night their glad festival keep,
lines.gloss: führen = 'lead' (führen); den nächtlichen Reihn = 'the nightly round-dance' (accusative).

lines.original: Und wiegen und tanzen und singen dich ein."
lines.english: They'll dance thee, and rock thee, and sing thee to sleep."
lines.gloss: wiegen = 'rock, cradle'; tanzen = 'dance'; singen dich ein = 'sing thee to sleep' (einsingen, separable).
